results.reason: Issue 3 cites SA § 2.2, describes the automatic five-year renewals and the 270/240-day notice requirement, and calls it effectively a 30-day window. It says missing that window locks Harrowgate in for five more years.

Issue 4 quotes § 3.1 as covering all glass and PET containers for any beverage product, worldwide. It contrasts this with Term Sheet § 2.1 (amber glass, beer brands, U.S./Canada) and states the executed text controls.

Issue 1 notes receipt on August 3, 2026 and calculates that the window expired September 2, 2026, 19 days before the September 21 Amendment. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted and seeks an express extension or waiver.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment § 2 replaces § 11.2, deletes the Recall carve-out and limits the indemnity carve-out to § 9.1(c) IP claims. It says recall and product-liability exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

Issue 5 covers new § 14.4, which allows assignment to Affiliates and successors without consent, notwithstanding § 14.3. It notes there is no competitor exclusion and that the restriction is now one-sided because Harrowgate still needs consent.
The Summary states that under SA § 15.2 written amendments take precedence and the Amendment controls where it conflicts with the SA.
Issue 2 quotes § 11.1: the cap is 'the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.'
The memo is addressed to [Supervising Partner] and takes the issues one at a time. Each issue has a Location line and a Recommended fix.
The memo proposes specific language for a restored § 11.2, a narrowed § 3.1, a revised § 2.2 and a § 14.4 with a competitor exclusion.
The memo states that Harrowgate cannot now serve a timely objection and that the window closed before the Amendment date.
The memo says the executed text controls and that the Term Sheet is non-binding and superseded.
